items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: The interviewee mentions Louis Armstrong only as a band that played at the Springfield State Fair ('Louis Armstrong had a big band come through') and in response to the interviewer's prompt 'Louis Armstrong?' with 'Pops.' There is no evidence of personal interaction, collaboration, or direct acquain

ctx.x: Who else was on that date?

Ernie Henry -- on the side I was on, I think a pianist named Al Knight, and I think he had Arthur Taylor on the drums. On that side, I mean, on that record that Jazz by Gee they called it, I think. And Frank Foster and some others on the other side.

But that was the first thing I did for Riverside. And as I started playing around New York out in Brooklyn ... Kenny Dorham, Ernie Henry, people like that -- word of mouth gets around, you know, and like when you work, everybody starts calling you.

items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: I know Les Louis Armstrong was there.

ctx.x: tenor drum, and my home made fiddle. We had a fellow named Jake who played piano. Yeah, there was a piano. And we'd go out hustling from tavern to tavern and roadhouse to roadhouse, plus we played amateur shows all around Chicago. And win. The prize was $3, and I guess we had 8 pieces, but that was a nice piece of money during that time.

We also played the Savoy Ballroom. They had a barn-dance and they had a tramp band contest. Well, the Chicago Maniacs came out on top; maybe if some old Chicagoans could remember those days ... The Riviera Theatre used to have amateur shows -- I think this was during the time; I don't know, when was the time of that first flood? Wasn't it in Pennsylvania, a big flood, and they had benefits all over the country, and they had a benefit at the Riviera Theatre. I know Les Louis Armstrong was there.

And we played. That tramp band was something. And from the tramp band, the fellows started using guitars, trios and quartets, singing some barbershop harmony, and doing tunes like "China Boy" and "Chinatown" and "Tiger Rag". And I'm still playing this home made fiddle. At the same time, I'm going to school.
